Re: Joint Representation and Conflict of Interest Waiver — Formation and Operating Agreement for Kestrel Grove Bakery LLC

Dear Priya and Daniel:

You have each asked this firm to represent both of you, together with Kestrel Grove Bakery LLC (the "Company"), in connection with the formation of the Company and the negotiation and drafting of its operating agreement. Pennsylvania Rule of Professional Conduct 1.7 permits us to do so only if each of you gives informed consent, confirmed in writing, after we have explained the material risks of and reasonably available alternatives to the joint representation. This letter is that explanation, and your signature at the end is that consent.

1. Scope of the Joint Representation. We will represent Priya Raghunathan, Daniel Ostrowski, and the Company jointly in (a) forming the Company under the Pennsylvania Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, (b) preparing and negotiating the operating agreement, and (c) preparing the related organizational consents and membership certificates. We are not representing any of you in any other matter, and we are not advising any of you on personal tax, estate, or family-law consequences of the arrangements described in the operating agreement.

2. Common Interest at the Outset. At present your interests appear to be aligned: each of you wishes to form the Company promptly, on economically balanced terms, at the lowest reasonable cost. A joint representation is ordinarily more efficient and less expensive than separate counsel, and it avoids the adversarial posture that separate counsel can introduce into a founding relationship.

3. Actual and Potential Conflicts. Your interests are not identical, and on several questions they are directly opposed. Every additional percentage point of membership interest allocated to one of you is a percentage point taken from the other. The vesting schedule, the buy-sell price, the definition of "cause" for removal, the size of the initial capital contributions, the treatment of the recipe portfolio each of you brings, and the scope of any non-competition covenant are all provisions on which what is favorable to one of you is unfavorable to the other. If a dispute arises between you, whether now or after the Company is operating, we would be required to withdraw from representing any of you in that dispute.

4. No Confidentiality Between You. This is the most important consequence and the one clients most often misunderstand. In a joint representation there is no attorney-client privilege between the jointly represented clients. Anything either of you tells us that is material to this matter will be shared with the other, and we cannot agree to keep a material fact from one of you at the other's request. If you are not willing to accept that, you should not consent to the joint representation. As against third parties, the privilege remains intact and we will assert it.

5. Waiver of Future Conflict and Withdrawal. If a conflict arises that we cannot cure, we will withdraw from the joint representation. Each of you agrees that in that event we may continue to represent the Company alone, and that neither of you will seek to disqualify us from doing so on the basis of the joint representation or of information learned in it. We will not thereafter represent either of you individually against the other.

6. Reasonably Available Alternatives. You are each entitled to separate counsel, and you may retain separate counsel at any time, including now. You may also proceed with separate counsel for the negotiation of the operating agreement and return to us jointly for the ministerial formation filings. We encourage each of you to consult independent counsel about this letter itself before signing it, and you should take whatever time you need to do so.

7. Fees. Our fees for this matter will be billed at the rates set out in our engagement letter of even date and will be paid by the Company. The Company's payment of the fees does not make the Company our only client, and it does not alter the duties we owe each of you.

8. Consent. By signing below, each of you confirms that you have read this letter, that you have had the opportunity to ask us questions about it and to consult independent counsel about it, that you understand the material risks described in paragraphs 3 through 5, and that you consent to the joint representation on the terms stated.

Very truly yours,

HALLORAN & WEISS LLP
